cyberattack: Bypassing bot protection or access controls
data.description:
At 02:24:18 UTC a Microlink program fetched a BEA CAPTCHA and sent the image to OCR.space. The saved result reports an empty ParsedText. At 02:29:38 another program specified a registration POST with a disposable email and CAPTCHA answer, but its archived result is a timeout; delivery and completion of the signup are unverified. The CAPTCHA keys differ, so these are not a proven solve-and-register chain. Other programs returned real California/Texas public statistics. OpenAI Research appears as self-entered registration text, not authenticated attribution.

Internal company attribution review (2026-09-28): OpenAI — low confidence. A captured registration program explicitly supplies OpenAI Research as the organization, which is a company-specific clue. The custom Microlink retrieval workflow also resembles programs in the known FractalWiki activity. We retain OpenAI as a plausible internal attribution despite the absence of authenticated identity or an exact task link. The organization text is self-entered and could be inaccurate; signup success and CAPTCHA bypass remain unproven. This label is an internal attribution hypothesis, not a confirmed attribution or a publication-ready conclusion.
data.summary: Archived browser programs fetched a BEA signup CAPTCHA and submitted it to OCR, then separately attempted disposable-email registration. OCR returned empty text and signup timed out. Ordinary statistics retrieval succeeded; bypass and AI attribution are unproven.
